text:
sara_cs: flagging Phoenix onboarding - after they turned on SDK prefetch (prefetch_multiplier=3) for faster cold responses, they're seeing short bursts of 429s when their fleet scales. started when they went from 20 -> 180 warmers. attaching logs from their side.

sara_cs: sample (from customer):
```
2026-05-12T16:02:11Z INFO req=aa1 POST /v1/chat 200 time=102ms
2026-05-12T16:02:11Z WARN req=aa2 POST /v1/chat 429 time=16ms x-rate-limit-remaining=0
2026-05-12T16:02:11Z INFO req=aa3 POST /v1/chat 200 time=98ms
```

sara_cs: they also prefetch 3 completions per request (sdk prefetch) and each warmer does a fresh auth call per invocation. auth returns a short ttl (20s).

leo_se: thanks - two interacting anti-patterns: 1) prefetch_multiplier multiplies per-warm concurrency (each invocation issues N parallel requests) 2) ephemeral auth per invocation -> validation spike. combined they blow past our early per-tenant concurrency checks.

leo_se: quick mitigations for Phoenix: a) set prefetch_multiplier=1 on warmers b) cache tokens in-process for ttl-3s c) reuse connections via persistent pool d) add random startup splay for warmers so they don't all prefetch at the same instant.

mike_engineer: confirmed we saw the same signal in staging when we simulated 150 warmers with prefetch>1. short-lived tokens + parallel prefetch = auth validation storm. example python patch we gave them: 
```python
# reduce prefetch + token lease cache
_session = requests.Session()
_cache = {'t':None,'e':0}

def get_token():
    if time.time() < _cache['e'] - 3:
        return _cache['t']
    r = requests.post('https://auth.phoenix.app/mint')
    d = r.json()
    _cache.update({'t':d['token'],'e':time.time()+d['ttl']})
    return _cache['t']

# on init for warmers add splay
import random, time
time.sleep(random.uniform(0,1.2))
# ensure sdk config: prefetch_multiplier=1, connection_pool_size=16
```

jess_support: I'll ask Phoenix to flip prefetch_multiplier to 1 for their production warmers as a 10% canary. also asking them to enable our SDK's persistent connection option.

infra_bot: mitigation ticket #CS-6102 opened by jess_support. owner=leo_se expires_in=25m playbook=reduce-prefetch-token-cache

mike_engineer: aside: we can add a gateway-derived hint header for tenants who opt in: `x-auth-pressure-level: 0|1|2` where 2 = sustained auth bursts; useful for their SRE alerting. I'll file a small feature task.

sara_cs: customer tested local changes in staging: 429 rate dropped from 9.2% -> 0.8% within 12m after switching prefetch->1 and adding token cache. they will roll a 10% prod canary.

leo_se: note for SDK docs: highlight prefetch_multiplier interaction with serverless warmers and short auth TTLs. add explicit example for token-lease/caching and recommend default prefetch=1 for serverless environments.

jess_support: plan: 1) canary at 10% with prefetch=1 + token cache 2) monitor 429s and x-rate-limit-* 3) if stable for 30m, ramp -> 100% and update onboarding checklist.

sara_cs: capturing this in renewal/health notes: customer was nervous about prefetch as a performance tweak; resolving this increased their confidence.

infra_bot: #CS-6102 status=monitoring owner=leo_se

sara_cs: 40m update: canary healthy, Phoenix completed 100% ramp. closing in 24h if no regression. thanks team :rocket:
